# AGENTS.md

Build, test, and run instructions for this repository (nothing else belongs in this file).

- Requires Node.js >= 22 and npm. Install dependencies: `npm ci`.
- One npm package (`xspec`) holding two distinct programs: the product under `src/` and the test harness under `test/`. The harness never imports product code; it drives the built `xspec` executable as a subprocess.
- Build the product: `npm run build` — compiles `src/` (TypeScript ESM, `src/tsconfig.json`) to `dist/`; the `xspec` bin is `dist/cli/bin.js`. Run it: `node dist/cli/bin.js`. A hand-staged scratch workspace (an `xspec.config.ts` plus sources, anywhere on disk) needs no `node_modules`: the product resolves the configuration's `import … from "xspec"` itself, so `cd <workspace> && node /abs/path/to/dist/cli/bin.js build --json` works as is — the quickest way to eyeball a finding's exact location before pinning it in a test. A ready-made configuration for such a workspace is the `E6_CONFIG` template literal in `test/helpers/e6.ts` (main specs under `specs/**/*.mdx`, code under `src/**/*.ts`): copy it verbatim into `xspec.config.ts`. For a baseline-taking command (`impact --base <ref>`, `review create --base <ref> --name <n>`) the scratch workspace must also be a git repository holding the ref: `git init`, an identity (`git config user.email` and `user.name` — the harness's isolated git configuration does not apply to hand staging), `git add -A && git commit`; a `.xspec/journal` committed at the ref is the baseline's journal, and the working copy's uncommitted edits are the current workspace.
- The built product enables Node's on-disk V8 compile cache (`node:module` `enableCompileCache`; default directory under the OS temp dir, e.g. `/tmp/node-compile-cache`). The first invocations after `npm run build` repopulate it, so one-off CLI timings are slower than steady state; the cache affects timing only, never output. Steady-state per-invocation medians on this sandbox at FIX_PLAN Task 7 of the Phase 10 plan written at 6694886 (a two-file spec workspace with a current store): `version` ~66 ms, `inventory` ~220 ms, and ~345–395 ms for every command that analyzes the sources — `at` and `query` included, which no longer answer from the store (Task 7 retired that fast path: ~185 ms before, the read SPEC 13.3 forbids). That cost is mostly module loading: Node's start ~35 ms; the TypeScript compiler ~120 ms (loaded through `createRequire` in `src/core/ts-module.ts` — importing that CJS file through the ESM loader instead costs ~0.2 s more per invocation in format sniffing and named-export lexing; keep any new `typescript` use routed through that module); the MDX toolchain ~75 ms and the product's own modules ~35 ms; then the configuration's parse ~20 ms (its syntax check reads a no-emit single-file program's diagnostics — `ts.transpileModule` spent ~65 ms there, mostly on an emit nothing read) and the analysis, derivation, and store comparison ~55 ms. A module statically imported from `src/cli/main.ts` loads for every command, `version` included (the fast path's imports cost each ~110 ms) — the numbers that matter when a test sweeping many CLI invocations nears its timeout.
- Typecheck both programs: `npm run typecheck` (`src/tsconfig.json`, then `test/tsconfig.json`; the harness is not typechecked by Vitest at run time). `test/fixtures/` is excluded from the harness typecheck: fixture projects are data compiled or executed at test run time and may contain deliberate type errors (e.g. the S-4 fixture project's `type-error.ts`, `import-conflict.ts`, `import-duplicate.ts`, and `companion-error.d.ts`, and its five module-settings detection modules — `export-assignment.ts`, `import-assignment.ts`, `type-reexport.ts`, `type-import.ts`, and `top-level-await.ts` — each rejected under one of TEST-SPEC H-2's two configurations and accepted under the other).
- Consumer fixture programs are compiled through the harness's TypeScript tooling driver (`test/helpers/tooling.ts`), whose compiler and language service are the harness's own devDependency `typescript-5.9.3` — `npm ci` (dev dependencies included) must have run for consumer compilation to work. The driver serves TEST-SPEC H-2's two fixed configurations and nothing else: `COMMONJS_CONFIGURATION` (`strict`, `target` ESNext, `module` CommonJS under its default `node10` resolution) and `ES_MODULE_CONFIGURATION` (`strict`, `target` ESNext, `module` ESNext, `moduleResolution` bundler, `isolatedModules`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`), every other option at TypeScript 5.9.3's default — no `skipLibCheck`, `types`, or `typeRoots`. `ConsumerProject.load({ rootDir, rootFiles, configuration })` requires one of the two exactly and refuses any other option (a plain `Error`); `forEachConsumerProject` loads and asserts under each in turn, every diagnosis naming its configuration; verdicts `assertTypeChecksClean` (no diagnostic of any category anywhere in the program, generated modules and companions included) and `assertTypeErrorsAt` (every diagnostic at an expected position, each position covered by an error); runtime `withCompiledConsumer(project, context, (compiled) => compiled.run("src/app.ts"))`, under the CommonJS configuration alone. The NodeNext path the driver kept until the plan written at 2a2b94e's FIX_PLAN Task 27 (`defaultConsumerCompilerOptions`, an unconfigured project, `assertNoCompileErrors`, `assertCompileErrorAt`, `ConsumerProject.emit`, `ConsumerProject.errors`, an exported `runConsumer`) is gone, so no consumer reaches another configuration. Under H-2 nothing supplies `@types/node`: a consumer program writes through `console.log` / `console.error` (ESNext's default library declares `console`) or declares what it reads of `process` itself (`declare const process: { readonly argv: readonly string[] };`, module-scoped in a file holding an import or export). A project's root, and the runtime output directory, must have no `node_modules` entry in any ancestor (`HarnessStagingError`, mode `consumer-isolation`, otherwise), so a fixture project under this repository is compiled from a copy in a `TestWorkspace` (S-4's `stageFixtureProject`), never in place. Each program checks the default library too: about 0.25 s to build and 0.45 s to check a small program on this machine, so a verdict under both configurations costs about 1.4 s, and the S-4 file's 49 tests take ~45 s alone (43.6 s at that Task 27). The runtime output is the compiler's alone — the program's CommonJS JavaScript, the project root's layout kept below it — written into a fresh `xspec-consumer-out-*` directory under the OS temporary directory, outside the workspace, run there under plain Node, and removed afterwards: the built product's runtime companion `NAME.xspec.impl.js`, a product-written file beside `NAME.xspec.impl.d.ts`, is no compiler output, so from that plan's Task 23 on a consumer of the built product type-checks clean under both configurations while its compiled run fails with `Cannot find module './A.xspec.impl.js'` (exit 1) — the migrated runtime arms meet that diagnosed until the product changes. Every consumer test takes H-2's configurations: since that plan's Task 24 the §1–§2 consumer tests (`section-1.1-1.2.ts`, `section-1.4.ts`, `section-1.6-1.7.ts`, `section-2.4.ts`: every verdict through `forEachConsumerProject`, T1.1-2's skeleton reads through `forEachConfiguration` with a project loaded per configuration, each runtime arm a CommonJS project's `withCompiledConsumer`), since its Task 25 the §4 consumer tests (`section-4.ts`, `section-4.1-4.2.ts`, `section-4.3-4.4.ts`, `section-4.5.ts`: T4-3, T4-4, T4.1-1–T4.1-3, T4.2-3, T4.2-4 — its definitions and hovers under each configuration too — T4.3-1, T4.4-1, T4.4-2, and T4.5-1, every stdout-writing consumer declaring `process` as T1.2-2's does; T4.4-1's facet-4 consumer, carrying its expected type error, still compiles through `withCompiledConsumer`, a semantic diagnostic being no emit diagnostic), since its Task 26 T13.1-2 (`section-13.1-13.2.ts`: its clean verdict, missing-path type error, definitions, and hovers under each configuration in turn through `forEachConfiguration`, a project loaded per configuration, before its CommonJS runtime arm), and since its Task 27 the §6.5 and §14 consumers (`section-6.5.ts`'s T6.5-9, `section-6.5-ii.ts`'s T6.5-11 — its (d) one type-error assertion at the type alias's `O` alone — `section-6.5-iii.ts`'s T6.5-18, `section-6.5-v.ts`'s T6.5-23(c), and `section-14.ts`'s T14-2 — its two unresolved references one type-error assertion — every premise and post-move compile under each configuration through `forEachConsumerProject`); against the built product T1.2-2 and T1.6-3 (since Task 24), T4-3, T4.1-3, T4.3-1, T4.4-1, T4.4-2, and T4.5-1 (since Task 25), T13.1-2 (since Task 26), and T4.1-1 (since Task 36, at its built-in-member runtime arm, past every type-level arm) fail diagnosed at their first runtime arm's exit code (exit 1, `Cannot find module './<NAME>.xspec.impl.js'`; ~2.4 s and ~5.5 s, 2.6–5.5 s, ~3.5–4.7 s, and ~7.7 s, alone), every other consumer test passing (Task 27's five: T6.5-9 ~7 s, T6.5-11 ~30 s, T6.5-18 ~20 s, T6.5-23 ~57 s, T14-2 ~4 s, alone).
- Two copies of TypeScript 5.9.3 (the release SPEC 14.20 fixes) are installed: the product's `typescript` dependency, pinned exactly, and the harness's own devDependency `typescript-5.9.3`, an npm alias of `typescript@5.9.3`. Harness code imports `typescript-5.9.3`, never `typescript` — the tooling driver and S-4 do, and so must S-9's TypeScript well-formedness check (its parser must be a harness dependency independent of the product) and any other harness use; product code keeps reaching `typescript` through `src/core/ts-module.ts`. npm cannot list one package name in both dependency sets (the devDependencies entry would replace the product's), hence the alias. After a clean `npm ci`, `node_modules/.bin/tsc` is the product's copy; an incremental `npm install` may relink it to the alias — the bytes are identical either way.
- Full test suite (TEST-SPEC sections 1–17, certification included; the Linux CI leg): `npm test`. Build the product first — tests invoke the built executable. Without a build (`dist/cli/bin.js` absent), every product-facing test fails as a diagnosed `HarnessAssertionError` naming that path, before anything is spawned (H-8's no-product run: `builtProductBinding()` in `test/helpers/subprocess.ts` sets `missingFilesFailDiagnosed`, so its missing artifact is the missing product; `builtProductBindingAt(<path>)` is the same binding at another artifact path), each `checkProperty` property (P-1 to P-14) reported as drawn at its first trial with its seed, never shrunk (the failure declines shrinking); any other binding's missing file — a certification fixture's, the S-7 stub's, a compiled consumer's, a temporary runner's scratch build — stays a plain-`Error` harness error (C-1: an unbuilt fixture is a harness defect, never a certified failure), which the certification runner reports as `error`. Measured at the affd85f plan's FIX_PLAN Task 4, under `unshare --map-user` with `NODE_OPTIONS` unset: `test/suite/section-1.1-1.2.test.ts`, `section-16-p1.test.ts`, and `e6-exchange-writer.test.ts` with no build ran 8 tests, all failing so (P-1 "falsified with seed 271828183 (trial 1 of 25)", reported as drawn), in 6.71 s; the certification runner over every registered body and S-7's six layer-4 bodies against `builtProductBindingAt(<an absent path>)` ended 352 and 6 `fail`, every diagnosis naming the path, in 7.9 s, and against the unflagged binding of the same shape 348 and 6 `error`, with `fail` for T7-5, T13.4-12, T13.5-6, and P-14 alone (their own conversions of a run's rejection wrap the message).

T13.5-2 (`test/suite/registry/section-13.5.ts`) runs on the default 120 s `timeoutMs`: from the 772854b plan's FIX_PLAN Task 15 on a full pass drives about 57 product invocations — the held workspace's staging, ten refusals, and five runs after command 1, two determinism repeats (nine each), and five unheld twins (four each) — 21 of them mutating runs that complete (each lengthened by any post-release dwell, VIOL-CORE-EARLYRELEASE's included) and 20 refused at acquisition; it took 3.7–5.2 s against the CONF-CORE fixtures that pass it, an estimated ~20 s for a conforming built product at the built product's ~0.33 s per invocation, and the 13.5-pre-revision built product fails it at its first held inspection in ~1.3 s. T13.5-3 (`test/suite/registry/section-13.5.ts`) runs on the default 120 s `timeoutMs` too: from the 772854b plan's FIX_PLAN Task 16 on a full pass drives about 68 product invocations — five kill-while-held trials of five runs each (the session staging's `build`, `review create`, and `review status`, the held run killed, the later command), the past-the-hold base's three staging runs, five twins, and seven kills per command (`PAST_THE_HOLD_KILL_FRACTIONS`, 35 in all) — and took 6.2–6.8 s alone against the CONF-CORE fixtures that pass it (8.5 s against VIOL-CORE-PARTIALWRITE, whose 50 ms derived-file intervals stretch `rename`'s and `move`'s lift-to-exit spans to ~134 ms); VIOL-CORE-EARLYRELEASE fails it at its first past-the-hold kill in ~14.4 s, VIOL-CORE-STALELOCK at its first later command in ~0.4 s, and the 13.5-pre-revision built product at its first held kill (`found nothing at .xspec/lock`) in ~1.3 s; an estimated ~30–40 s for a conforming built product at ~0.33 s per invocation. The CONF-CORE conformer's lift-to-exit spans run ~25–45 ms for all five mutating commands (its hold file polled every 15 ms), so its kills land before the last write, after it, and after the exit — every branch of the arm. VIOL-CORE-EARLYRELEASE's 1 s dwell (`EARLY_RELEASE_DWELL_MS` in `test/fixtures/conf-core/product.mjs`) lengthens every mutating run that acquires: against it T13.5-2 took ~25 s, T13.5-1 ~14 s, T13.5-8 ~6 s (~11 s from the 772854b plan's FIX_PLAN Task 20 on, ~14 s from its Task 21 on), T6.1-2, T10.4-5, and T13.4-5 ~4 s each, run one at a time. - Run a subset of a test project by appending file paths, e.g. `npx vitest run --config test/vitest.config.ts --project suite test/suite/section-1.1-1.2.test.ts` — the way to observe new product-facing tests failing-as-diagnosed against the stub product (Phase 9 red-green). Append `--reporter=verbose` to see each test's duration — the quick check that a many-invocation sweep (e.g. T6.1-1's ~34 CLI runs, ~9 s at steady state) actually drove every arm rather than short-circuiting. Vitest's `-t <pattern>` name filter narrows further but matches substrings of the whole title, so filtering on a test ID (`-t "T6.5-5"`) also runs every test whose title cites that ID (T6.5-4's title mentions T6.5-5, adding its ~9 s) — read the verbose list to see what actually ran. To select one registered test inside a file, add `-t '<ID> '` with a trailing space (Vitest's name filter is a regex over the declared name `<id> <title>`, so `-t 'T6\.5-1 '` runs T6.5-1 alone, not T6.5-10 through T6.5-19).
- Running tests also requires the system `git` executable on PATH: harness fixtures script local git repositories (`test/helpers/workspace.ts`). No git configuration is needed — the builder isolates all ambient git config and identity. The builder's `gitInit`/`gitCommitAll` serve the workspace root's repository only; a nested repository (T6.3-5's stagings in `test/suite/registry/section-6.3.ts`, its nested-repository one shared with T6.3-6(b) and (e) through `stageNestedRepositories`) is scripted through the public `git([...])` with `-C <subdir>` and an inline `-c user.name=… -c user.email=…` identity (the isolated environment has none), and `git -c protocol.file.allow=always submodule --quiet add ./<subdir> <subdir>` registers an already-initialized in-place repository as a submodule without cloning (the gitlink is staged; `.git` stays a directory) — the `protocol.file.allow` override is what git 2.38+ demands for a local-path submodule. The Linux leg's lock-path leftover stagings (`stageLeftover` in `test/helpers/lock-staging.ts`) and its FIFO staging at any other path whose parent directory stands (`stageFifo`, the same route; T6.3-6(c)'s `.xspec/journal`, since the plan written at 2a2b94e's FIX_PLAN Task 48) also need coreutils' `mkfifo` on PATH: Node has no API for FIFOs, so each is made by `mkfifo -m <mode>` under an ASCII name in a scratch directory beside the workspace root (the `TestWorkspace`'s `tempRoot`) and hard-linked into place, which never replaces an occupant and takes a name that is not valid UTF-8 as its bytes; a missing or failing `mkfifo` is a `HarnessStagingError` (mode `lock-path-leftover`), never a skip. TEST-SPEC H-1's ancestor precondition (`assertSelfContainedRoot`, `test/helpers/self-contained-root.ts`, since the plan written at 2a2b94e's FIX_PLAN Task 21) runs git too, and it requires the OS temporary directory (`os.tmpdir()`, so `TMPDIR`) to lie inside no git working tree, with no entry named `xspec.config.ts` in any directory above it: before every arm presuming nothing above its workspace root — T7-1's failed upward search, T12.7-3's `.`-path arm, T6.3-5(c), T12.0-12's sweep, T13.5-8's two baseline arms, T11.6-4's arm B, T12.6-2's no-configuration context, and T12.0-14's `--config`-first premise (T6.3-6(b), T14-10(k), and T13.5-8's journal-staged baseline arms call it as they land) — it `lstat`s `xspec.config.ts` in every directory above the root, along the root's spelling and its physical path, and asks `git -C <root> rev-parse --show-toplevel` under the environment the driver gives the product (`productEnvironment`, `test/helpers/subprocess.ts`) with `LC_ALL=C`, only git's "not a git repository" verifying the repository half; an unmet or unverified half is a `HarnessStagingError` (mode `self-contained-root`), a harness error, never a pass or a product failure, so a run with `TMPDIR` inside a repository or below a stray `xspec.config.ts` errors exactly those tests (to check by hand: run them through a temporary runner — the bullet beginning "To run a selection of product tests against one fixture executable" — with `TMPDIR` set to a directory below one holding an empty `xspec.config.ts`, or inside a scratch `git init` repository: each ends `error`, its diagnosis the staging error naming the entry or the working tree; the scratch trees go in the scratchpad, never in the checkout, which is itself a working tree).
- Harness self-tests and certification only (TEST-SPEC 17): `npm run test:self`, which needs no product build (TEST-SPEC H-8: self-tests and certification pass before the product exists); CI's harness-self job runs it with no `dist/`. Its S-7 file, `test/self/s7-red-green-sweep.test.ts`, sweeps every product-facing body (the registered ones and the seven layer-4 bodies outside the registry, T7-1's single-casing probe, synthetic entry T99.7-8, the seventh from the plan written at 2a2b94e's FIX_PLAN Task 54 on) against the empty stub and, from the affd85f plan's FIX_PLAN Task 5 on, against an absent built-product artifact as well (`builtProductBindingAt(<dist/cli/bin.js inside a fresh temporary directory>)`, absent whatever the checkout's `dist/` holds, so it checks the same with or without a build), each body required to fail diagnosed, every no-product diagnosis naming the artifact (the file's 7 tests took 30.95 s alone under `unshare --map-user` at that Task, 7.1 s of it the no-product registry sweep). Its certification runner prints one `PASS`/`FAIL` line per (test, fixture) pair as it drives each fixture executable; a violator's `FAIL` lines are its expected outcomes, not failures — Vitest's own failures are the `×` lines and the final `Tests` summary, so when piping the output through `grep`, filter on those rather than on `FAIL` (the runner's lines are indented — `  FAIL  T…` — so a line-anchored `grep -v '^FAIL '` does not drop them; match `×` and the `Tests` summary instead, and never cap the output with `head -N`: the runner's 30-odd per-pair lines precede the summary, so redirect the run to a log file and grep that afterwards). To certify one fixture family alone, filter `test/self/certification.test.ts` on the family name every one of its test titles carries: `npx vitest run --config test/vitest.config.ts --project self test/self/certification.test.ts -t CORE` runs the CONF-CORE conformer and each VIOL-CORE-* violator (~150 s in all from the 772854b plan's FIX_PLAN Task 21 on — 149.93 s, and 152.84 s with `--reporter=verbose`, whose per-verification times were the conformer's 8.5 s, VIOL-CORE-NOLOCK's 7.8 s, VIOL-CORE-EARLYWRITE's 8.0 s, VIOL-CORE-EARLYREFRESH's 9.1 s, VIOL-CORE-STALELOCK's 6.1 s, VIOL-CORE-PARTIALWRITE's 10.2 s, VIOL-CORE-CHATTYREADS's 8.0 s, VIOL-CORE-PERSISTREADS's 8.4 s, VIOL-CORE-LATEHOLD's 8.7 s, VIOL-CORE-EARLYRELEASE's 29.2 s, VIOL-CORE-HOLDLINK's 16.6 s, VIOL-CORE-READERENTRY's 8.0 s, and VIOL-CORE-BUILDWAIT's 18.3 s, 146.9 s summed, its T13.5-8 driving 10 more product invocations per fixture than before; - The self project — and, once the Linux-leg tests (T13.5-7, T14-9, T14-10, T13.5-8 since its acquisition-after arms' unlistable `specs/sub`, T13.5-10 since its permission removals, T13.4-12 since its unreadable leftovers' `--x` lock directory and `-w-------` entry, T13.5-11 since its `-wx` and `r-x` stagings during holds and its T13.5-7 write refusals, T13.5-12 since its `--x` `specs/sub` during holds, and P-15 since its leftover plain files with every permission removed, each verified refused on the harness itself) are registered, the suite project — must run as an unprivileged identity. The permission-based stagings of environment refusals (`test/helpers/permissions.ts`; TEST-SPEC E-1) verify themselves on the harness's own process before any product is invoked and throw `HarnessStagingError` — a harness error, never a diagnosed product failure — when the runner is privileged: root, or any identity holding CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE, writes into a read-only directory and reads a mode-0o200 file, so `test/self/permission-staging.test.ts` fails as root by design, as do the six tests of `test/self/lock-path.test.ts` that stage a mode refusing this process's own read or write (H-4's grant-and-restore under `.xspec/lock`) and verify it first, and the one test of `test/self/lock-staging.test.ts` that stages leftover plain files with every permission removed, whose staging verifies the removal on this process and throws `HarnessStagingError` when its own read succeeds, the two tests of `test/self/lock-state.test.ts` that first verify on this process the refused read of a mode-0o000 entry and the refused listing of a mode-0o300 (`-wx`) directory in the lock directory, and the one test of `test/self/s3-subprocess-driver.test.ts` that runs a stand-in from a working directory staged mode 000 once entered (`runProductInEnteredDirectory`, whose staging verifies itself through `stageDirectoryMode`) (never skip or work around it). CI runs both projects through `.github/scripts/run-without-network.sh`, which refuses root and a runner without passwordless sudo: it enters fresh network and mount namespaces as root through sudo and drops back to the caller's own uid, gid, and groups with every capability cleared, staying in the machine's user and process-identifier namespaces, so the command has no network, mode bits bite, and sudo still works there (the administrative access 13.5's machine-wide stagings need: T13.5-9's second user and second mount, T13.5-10(e)-(g)'s fresh process-identifier namespaces; TEST-SPEC E-1, H-2). It also restores the caller's environment and resource limits (sudo resets both), maps the host's name to loopback in a private `/etc/hosts` where the real one lacks it (sudo, built with fqdn, otherwise warns on stderr inside the network namespace), verifies all of it, and prints one `run-without-network.sh: uid ...` verification line, naming the temporary directory's filesystem type, before the command's output. In a root sandbox, reproduce its unprivileged identity alone with `unshare --map-user=1000 --map-group=1000 -- npm run test:self` (util-linux 2.38+: the command runs as uid 1000 with every capability cleared, while the repository's root-owned files stay owner-accessible, so git, npm, and Vitest's cache work unchanged — the whole self project takes the same ~2.5 min there). A plain non-root user needs no wrapper for that. sudo cannot work under these `unshare --map-user` recipes (no real root is mapped, so its set-user-ID bit is ignored), so tests needing administrative access fail there as harness errors. To reproduce CI's whole inner stage, administrative access included, run the wrapper itself as a non-root user with passwordless sudo from a copy of the checkout that user owns; in this sandbox that is `claude` (uid 999, gid 1001, NOPASSWD sudo): copy with `mkdir <copy> && tar --exclude=./.git -cf - . | tar -xf - -C <copy> && chown -R claude:claude <copy>`, then `sudo -n -u claude -H bash -c 'export PATH=/opt/node22/bin:$PATH && cd <copy> && git init -q && bash .github/scripts/run-without-network.sh env -u NODE_OPTIONS <command>'` (a `<copy>` under `/home/claude`), with `/opt/node22/bin` first because the `PATH` sudo gives `claude` (`/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin:/snap/bin`) finds `/usr/local/bin/node`, Node v20.20.2, where this repository and CI need Node 22: the wrapper hands the command the caller's environment, so `node --version` as the command prints v22.22.2 with the export and v20.20.2 without it. At 34df333 the whole self project took ~2 min this way and gave CI's result; at 4994dab, on Node 22, 124 s, with the same 2 failed / 4313 passed as the `unshare --map-user` recipe's 127 s run. This sandbox has no `ip`, so the wrapper's loopback bring-up is a no-op here, where CI's runner brings `lo` up. sudo also drops the sandbox's agent variables (`CLAUDECODE`, `AI_AGENT`), under which Vitest 4 (std-env's `isAgent`) prints plain text through its `agent` reporter, so this recipe's log is the default reporter's, with ANSI color escapes even when redirected to a file: strip them (`sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g'`) before grepping it for `×` or the `Tests` summary. Self-test files that need administrative access are named `*.admin.test.ts` (the first, from the 772854b plan's FIX_PLAN Task 11: `test/self/machine-staging.admin.test.ts`): CI runs them with the rest, and under the `unshare --map-user` recipes, where sudo cannot work, they fail as harness errors (`HarnessStagingError`, mode `administrative-access`), never skips. Where harness runs get no administrative access — this sandbox, whose permission system refuses sudo-related commands as credential exploration, so no recipe here, this one included, may run a test, staging, or script that needs it, nor inspect sudo, accounts, or credentials — run the self project with `--exclude 'test/self/**/*.admin.test.ts'` on the command line (never skip them in code) and verify those files in CI: push, then read that push's harness-self job before relying on the result (its check run's annotations, `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/check-runs/<job-id>/annotations`, list every failing test up to GitHub's cap of ten error annotations per step — run 1176's full-suite job, 22 tests failing, showed ten — so a job failing more is read from its log; its log comes through the GitHub MCP `get_job_logs` tool, `return_content` with `tail_lines` about 200 reaching the summary — the built-in `gh api` refuses the log's redirect). The same holds for registered product tests needing it (T13.5-9, T13.5-10(e)-(g)), which S-7's sweep also runs. The older nested recipe still reproduces the network-denied unprivileged stage, without sudo: nest the `unshare --map-user` wrapper in a fresh network namespace whose loopback is up: `unshare --map-root-user --net -- bash -c 'python3 <lo-up.py> && cd /home/user/xspec && unshare --map-user=1000 --map-group=1000 -- <command>'`. This sandbox has neither `ip` nor `ifconfig`, so `<lo-up.py>` is a five-line Python helper that ORs IFF_UP (1) into `lo`'s flags through `fcntl.ioctl` on an `AF_INET` datagram socket: `SIOCGIFFLAGS` (0x8913) reads them and `SIOCSIFFLAGS` (0x8914) writes them, each request `struct.pack('16sH14s', b'lo', flags, bytes(14))`. Inside, the command runs as uid 1000 with `CapEff` 0, loopback binds, names do not resolve, and the agent proxy is unreachable. CI's runners set no `NODE_OPTIONS` (neither `.github/workflows/ci.yml` nor `.github/scripts/run-without-network.sh` sets it, the hosted `ubuntu-24.04` image's README in `actions/runner-images` lists no such variable, and run 963's harness-self log never names it), so Node there runs with its default heap limit, about 2 GB, whereas this sandbox exports `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192` (an 8 GB heap), which reaches every command it starts, the namespaced ones included: to reproduce CI's heap limit as well, unset it inside the inner namespace — `unshare --map-user=1000 --map-group=1000 -- env -u NODE_OPTIONS <command>` (V8's `heap_size_limit` then reads 2096 MB, against 8240 MB with the sandbox's setting; the tenth plan's VERIFY at 7ef10b6 and its FIX_PLAN Task 10 ran this way). Hand-staging a permission refusal in a scratch workspace as root works only when the staging and the product run share one namespace invocation — `unshare --map-user=1000 --map-group=1000 -- bash -c 'cd <workspace> && chmod -R a-w .xspec && node /abs/path/to/dist/cli/bin.js build --json'` (or `chmod 0100 specs/sub` for an unlistable directory): inside it the mapped identity owns the root-created files and the cleared capabilities make the mode bits bite, whereas outside it root ignores them.
- Hang guards (TEST-SPEC S-3, with H-10, E-5, and §16's preamble; `test/helpers/hang-guards.ts`, since FIX_PLAN Task 18 of the plan written at 2a2b94e): the harness follows S-3's conservative design — a span carries no guard of its own. Every product invocation carries its own guard, the subprocess driver's hang guard (`RunOptions.timeoutMs`, default `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`, 30 s, overridden per call site), whose expiry kills the run and rejects it with `ProductRunTimeoutError`. No test, trial loop, property, shrink phase, certification verification, or sweep carries a time limit: every Vitest project's `testTimeout` is 0 (`test/vitest.config.ts`; Vitest 4.1.10 arms no timer for a timeout of 0 or less, `withTimeout` in `node_modules/@vitest/runner/dist/chunk-artifact.js`, and resolves a test's `timeout` with `??`, so an explicit 0 holds); registry entries name no `timeoutMs` (the field, its validation, and `DEFAULT_PRODUCT_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS` are gone); `declareProductTests`, the certification verifications, the S-7 sweeps, the E-6 writer, and the Windows leg's tests are declared with `NO_SPAN_GUARD` (0); no self-test passes a Vitest timeout (Vitest's 10 s `hookTimeout` still bounds `onTestFinished` cleanups); and the certification runner has no watchdog and no `testTimeoutMs` option — a temporary runner's own `{ timeout: … }` (the scratch patterns pass 7 200 000) bounds nothing but itself. A tripped guard ends its test: a body may convert the kill into a diagnosed failure (H-8; `runBounded`, `exitOf`, P-8's and P-11's command runners, unshrunk); the certification runner classifies a body ending with the kill unconverted — itself or as a `cause` in what it threw (`isHangGuardKill`, name fallback included) — as `hang` (it was `error`, `hang` having been the removed watchdog's), and `checkProperty` reports such a kill as a hang ("a product invocation did not terminate within its own hang guard while running trial N of M" or "while shrinking (on a shrunk input)", with the seed and the input, unshrunk, the kill its `cause`). A held run's guard covers its own work: once the harness finds the run's own hold standing — `RunningProduct.waitForFile` or `holdFileStands` on the `--test-hold` path its argv names (`holdPathArgument`, `test/helpers/invocation-grammar.ts`), resolved against its working directory and unoccupied as the run started — the guard is suspended until `releaseHoldFile` lifts that hold, then armed again for what is left of it (a held run's timeout then reads "timed out after N ms of its own hang guard, suspended while the harness kept its hold standing (TEST-SPEC S-3), and was killed"); so held runs take their module's ordinary per-run guard (`HELD_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS` in `section-13.5-iii.ts`, `-vi.ts`, and `-vii.ts`, `HELD_RESOLVE_TIMEOUT_MS` and `INTERFERENCE_HOLD_TIMEOUT_MS` in `section-13.5-ii.ts`, `HOLDER_TIMEOUT_MS` in `section-13.5-v.ts`, `E6_HELD_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS`, and `WINDOWS_HELD_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS` are gone; T13.5-13's held runs take its `RUN_TIMEOUT_MS`, 60 s), a hold observed by a harness's own `pathExists` polling suspends nothing (poll `holdFileStands`, as P-10's `holdsOrExits` and T13.5-13's `awaitExitedOrHolding` do), a lift must go through `releaseHoldFile`, and a hold path staged occupied keeps the run's guard running throughout (VIOL-CORE-HOLDLINK's dangling-link arm still fails T13.5-1 at `runBounded`'s 15 s). Counts bounding work — a property's shrink-execution cap, P-14's and P-15's shrink budgets, trial counts, P-10's `EXTRA_PRE_START_READS` — are no guards. Per-invocation guard sizing (since FIX_PLAN Task 19 of that plan): every per-invocation guard is at least ten times the longest the invocations it covers take, measured unloaded against the built product at the largest input their staging admits (H-11's scales: P-8's nesting floor, S-8's answer scale, P-11's fuzz), so `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` (30 s) covers every invocation but those whose call sites size their own — P-8's `FUZZ_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS` 60 s (its largest admitted answer, `view specs/B.mdx --text` over B with two balanced 4096-deep towers appended, 25.0 MB in 2.7–3.2 s at that Task, 3.8–5.0 s at the re-descent's second plan's Task 11), P-11's 300 s (raised at that Task from 120 s, which was 4.7× its largest admitted answer: `view --text specs/A.mdx` over A with two towers appended under the LF → U+2028 rewrite, 125.8 MB in 16.0–16.4 s at that Task and 25.4 s at that Task 11), T13.5-13's and P-14's `RUN_TIMEOUT_MS` 60 s, `runBounded`'s 15 s (`test/suite/registry/section-13.5.ts`), E-6's refused `move` 15 s (`E6_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS`; the Windows leg's whole E-6 subset runs in ~45 s), the second user's probe 120 s. A synchronous step that never returns is the one harness hang no guard ends: bounded construction rules it out, and CI's job limits (E-1: harness-self 20 min, full suite 90 min, Windows leg 30 min) bound it outside S-3's rule — a job cut at its limit, not a failed test — and locally nothing does: interrupt a run that stops progressing. mode `administrative-access`; a self-test stages access withheld through its `sudo` option, naming a stand-in command, never `sudo`); `ensureSecondUser()` (memoized per process: the account `xspec-second`, no home, its primary group the harness's own primary group, never removed, made by `sudo -n flock --wait 60 /run/lock/xspec-second-user.lock /bin/sh -c 'getent passwd "$1" > /dev/null || exec useradd …' sh xspec-second <gid>` — `useradd` checks the name before it locks the account files, so unserialized makers running at once both add it, the later overwriting the earlier's uid: CI run 1126 saw makers read uids 1003 and 1004; mode `second-user`); `stageGroupAccess(root)` (plain files g+rw, directories g+rwx, every harness-owned directory above the root g+x — a workspace's `mkdtemp` directory is 0700 — `restore()` reinstating each mode; what is made later keeps its maker's modes, so `.xspec` and the like must exist before the staging; mode `group-access`); `stageSecondMount(root, workspace.tempRoot)` (`sudo -n mount --bind` at `<tempRoot>/second-mount-<hex>`, verified through `/proc/self/mountinfo` — a bind mount shares its source's `st_dev` — and a probe file through either path; `remove()` unmounts with retries and removes the directory, and must run before the workspace's disposal; mode `second-mount`); `secondUserLauncher(user)`, a `RunLauncher` for `startProduct`'s `launcher` run option (`sudo -n -- /bin/sh -c 'umask "$1" && shift && exec "$@"' sh <umask> prlimit <every limit of the harness's process> -- setpriv --reuid=<uid> --regid=<gid> --init-groups --inh-caps=-all --bounding-set=-all -- env -i -- <the driver's environment> <command> <args>`; the command must be absolute and hold no `=`); `verifySecondUserReach(user, { root, createIn, binding })` (T13.5-9's verification: a probe run as the second user through the launcher, from a 0770 scratch directory under the temporary folder, lists every directory and reads every file under the root, creates and removes a file in each `createIn` directory, checks the binding's command executable and required files readable, and lists the harness's process while the harness lists the probe's) and `secondUserCreatesIn(user, dir)` (the same create check, unjudged); `reclaimForHarness(root)` (`sudo -n chown -R -h <uid> -- <root>`: every entry under the root, the root included, given to the harness's uid, no link followed, modes and groups untouched; T13.5-9 runs it after each run as the second user and before the workspace's disposal, so a product writing as the second user where it must be refused leaves nothing the harness cannot read or remove and still fails diagnosed; mode `second-user`). Hosted-runner facts (CI runs 1126 and 1127): sudo, with no terminal, forks the command directly into the process group it leads, so a launched run — always its own group — is killed whole by `sudo -n kill -s KILL -- -<group>`, which the driver's guards and `killGroup` use (the harness's own signal to those processes is `EPERM`, so `RunningProduct.kill` refuses a launched run); `killGroup` on a launched run also waits for every descendant its started process had (`descendantsOf` in `test/helpers/kill-discipline.ts`), so one that left the group fails as `ProcessGroupLingerError`; a launched run gets exactly the driver's environment (no `SUDO_*`), working directory, argv, umask, and limits, as the second user's uid and the shared gid (1001 there) with every capability set empty; Node, and the built product and the empty stub (`test/fixtures/empty-stub/bin.mjs`) in the checkout under `/home/runner/work`, are reachable by the second user (the verification's reach check passes there: the built product's in runs 1126 and 1127, the stub's in run 1216, Node executable and the stub readable). `test/self/machine-staging.admin.test.ts` checks the second user's reach against the harness-owned empty stub (`test/fixtures/empty-stub/bin.mjs`: Node executable, the stub readable, the stub never started), never the built product, so it needs no product build (H-8), while T13.5-9's own check reaches the built product it runs. H-6's run notes key a mutating run's lock path by the root path it was started under, so a run started through the second mount notes `<mount>/.xspec/lock`, not `<root>/.xspec/lock`.
- 13.5's machine-wide stagings, II (`test/helpers/machine-staging.ts`; TEST-SPEC H-2, E-1, E-3, T13.5-3, T13.5-10(e)-(g)): fresh process-identifier namespaces, made through sudo like stagings I, every failure `HarnessStagingError` of mode `pid-namespace` (or `administrative-access` first), never a skip. Each run started in one drops back to the harness's own uid, gid, and supplementary groups (`setpriv --reuid=<uid> --regid=<gid> --groups=<process.getgroups()>`, `--clear-groups` when there are none, `--inh-caps=-all --bounding-set=-all`, so every capability set is empty), with the harness's umask and resource limits and exactly the driver's environment (stagings I's root and `env -i` stages, shared). `freshNamespaceLauncher()` (launcher A; (f), (g)): `sudo -n -- /bin/sh -c 'umask "$1" && shift && exec "$@"' sh <umask> prlimit <limits> -- unshare --pid --fork --mount-proc -- setpriv ... -- env -i -- <env> <command> <args>`, so the run is identifier 1 of a namespace whose own `/proc` lists it alone (the working directory kept); verified once per process and sudo command by a probe run through it (a success remembered, a failure asked again). `openHarnessNamespace()` (launcher B; (e)'s run on another machine): the same `unshare` stage starting `/bin/bash --norc -c <NAMESPACE_FIRST_PROCESS_SCRIPT>` as the namespace's first process, verified fresh at open (`observe()` reads `{ listed: [1], lastAllocated: 1 }`); the script uses builtins alone, answering `observe` on its stdin with `observed <ns_last_pid> <listed>...` without forking, and bash's SIGCHLD handler reaps the orphans a namespace's first process adopts (a Node first process would not: libuv waits only for its own children). `--norc` is required: Node's stdio pipes are socketpairs, and a non-interactive bash whose stdin is a socket takes itself for a remote shell and sources `~/.bashrc` (here, under `unshare --map-user`, `/home/ubuntu/.bashrc: Permission denied` on stderr). Its `launcher` enters runs with `nsenter --target=<first process> --pid --mount --wdns=<cwd>` (entering a mount namespace resets the working directory to `/`; util-linux 2.39's `--wdns` resolves the directory inside, where `--wd` would keep one from the old mount namespace; mounts made after the namespace opened are not visible there); `close()` kills the first process's group through sudo and confirms it gone, the kernel ending every process in the namespace. Observations: `inNamespaceIdentifiers(run)` (the started process's and its descendants' `/proc/<pid>/status` NSpid lines, the field one level below the harness's own; a run with none is the staging error), `hasAllocated(observation, id)` for (e)'s reuse check, and the verifications `verifyNamespaceListsNone(namespace, ids, what)` ((e)) and `verifyListedByHarness(ids, what)` ((g)). Threads draw from the same identifiers as processes, so a namespace's `ns_last_pid` runs past its processes' identifiers (CI run 1130: a Node stand-in entered into a fresh harness namespace and its grandchild bore 9 at most, the last allocated 15), and a child process's in-namespace identifier comes after its parent's threads'. Hosted-runner facts (CI runs 1130 and 1131): every staging above works through the wrapper; two launcher-A runs of one stand-in bear the same in-namespace identifiers; the group kill through sudo reaches a namespace's first process from outside and empties the namespace, the hang guard's too. None of it runs in this sandbox (the directive above): `test/self/pid-namespace-staging.test.ts` pins locally the command lines, NSpid and answer parsing, `hasAllocated`, the first process's script run as a plain child, the (g) check, and the failure paths through stand-in sudo commands, one granting access but starting every command in the harness's own namespace among them; `test/self/pid-namespace-staging.admin.test.ts` runs in CI only.

So the product is the spawned process itself — its `process.ppid` the harness, only descriptors 0–2 open (`process.execve` discards every other descriptor itself), its environment exactly `productEnvironment(binding, options.env)` (no shell in between: `/bin/sh`, dash here, would add `PWD` and drop variables whose names are no shell identifiers) — with its own hang guard armed only as it starts (the wrapper's start, the staging, and the exec each a `guardStep`), and the staging is undone after the run, before T12.7-1's walk. The command must be an absolute path to an executable regular file (the exec searches no `PATH`; every binding uses `process.execPath`). A staging error surfaces as itself (`HarnessStagingError` on a privileged runner); anything else ending the run before the product starts — the wrapper's `{"failed":…}` report, or an exec the kernel refuses, which aborts Node with "process.execve failed with error code …" on stderr — is a harness error, never the product's outcome. Start each run a self-test awaits only when it awaits it: runs started together and awaited in turn let a later one reject — after the I/O each makes before its pre-flight — while an earlier one is still awaited, and Vitest then fails the whole run on that unhandled rejection though every test passes (`Errors  1 error`, exit 1; CI run 1421, the pre-flight refusals vector, whose table now starts each refused run inside its loop, from the plan written at 2a2b94e's FIX_PLAN Task 49). To judge such a test's other verdicts apart from that member against a build without it (any product before that Task 1), bind a scratch wrapper through the temporary-self-test pattern of the bullet above (scratchpad `t9j2_3/invlock.mjs`, run as `node invlock.mjs <mode> <binJs> <argv...>`; rebuild it from this description if it is gone): it runs `dist/cli/bin.js` through `spawnSync` with the invocation's argv, cwd, environment, and stdin, stderr inherited and stdout captured; where stdout parses as one JSON object carrying `graphData`, `journal`, and `sessions` and no `lock`, it inserts the single line `"lock": ".xspec/lock",` (two-space indent) before the line opening the top-level `"recorded"` member — the product prints canonical sorted-key two-space JSON, so every other byte is kept — re-parses the result to check it equals the original plus that member, writes it, and exits with the product's code (re-raising its signal). - Windows-leg subset (TEST-SPEC E-6; run by the Windows CI job): `npm run test:windows`. Build the product first. Its byte-identity test compares this leg's representative-fixture outputs against the Linux leg's, read from the directory named by `XSPEC_E6_EXCHANGE_DIR`; the Linux outputs are written by the suite project's E-6 writer test (`test/suite/e6-exchange-writer.test.ts`) whenever that variable is set during `npm test`, and CI exchanges them as the `e6-linux-outputs` artifact (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`). Against the stub product the whole subset is red (diagnosed failures) before any exchange is consulted; once the product conforms, run the Linux suite with the variable set, then the Windows subset with the same variable — with the variable unset or the directory absent, the byte-identity test fails loudly by design (never skips). The T11.6-1 drive-mismatch test (`test/windows/e6-drive-mismatch.test.ts`) additionally stages a substituted drive mapping (`subst`), which exists only on Windows: on any other platform it fails loudly after its same-drive premise arm (never skips), so a fully green `npm run test:windows` needs an actual Windows machine. The representative fixture (`runE6RepresentativeFixture` in `test/helpers/e6.ts`) runs 27 invocations, 26 of them recorded steps (~11.5 s against a product modelling 13.5's lock directory, and ~12 s against the built product, which passes it since FIX_PLAN Task 3 of the Phase 10 plan written at 6694886 moved its lock into `.xspec/lock`): after the file-form `move` and its `check`, step `move-section` moves `specs/sub/Moved.mdx#core.mid.tip` under `specs/Refs.mdx`'s `refs` as `refs.tip` (the built product adds `import Other from "./Other.xspec"` to Refs.mdx and `import Refs from "../specs/Refs.xspec"` to `src/app.ts`), `assertSectionMoveLanded` reads Refs.mdx's shape, and `check-post-section-move` follows; the section move stages nothing, so the fixture's S-9 records stay four. Its `rename` is E-6's exclusion probe (the 772854b plan's FIX_PLAN Task 48; `test/helpers/e6-exclusion.ts` holds the platform half, pinned by `test/self/e6-exclusion.test.ts`): `rename specs/Core.mdx core.mid.leaf core.mid.tip --test-hold <tempRoot>/e6-hold` is killed once held — on Linux by `killHeldRun` (T13.5-3's group kill), on Windows by `taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F` after the run's process tree is read from `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` (Windows PowerShell through `-EncodedCommand`, its standard input the null device; one `<pid> <ppid> <created>` line per process, then `END <count>`), each process then confirmed gone by identifier and creation time — after which `.xspec/lock` must hold one plain-file entry; the `rename` reruns as `… --test-hold ../e6-hold --json` (the hold path spelled relative to the root, so the recorded argv matches across legs), must take the leftover over (the held-state comparison, its one entry named apart from the dead run's), and while it holds `move specs/Core.mdx specs/sub/Moved.mdx --json` must exit 2 within 15 s with `code` `workspace-busy` and `path` `.xspec/lock`, the hold still standing, nothing modified, the entry again the only one; the transcript gains step `move-busy` (exit 2) before step `rename` (its performed-operation JSON); a `workspace-busy` refusal of the rerun runs T13.5-3's reuse check (Linux `/proc`, Windows the same PowerShell listing), a void rerunning from the byte snapshot taken before the kill (`.git` kept) up to 5 attempts; `.xspec/lock` is asserted absent after `rename`, `move`, `move-section`, `review-create`, and `review-resolve`, and the final tree excludes `.git` and `.xspec/lock`. Before that Task 3 the built product, its lock kept in the temporary folder, failed the fixture at the dead-entry assertion (`… after the kill, .xspec/lock is a directory holding exactly one entry …; found nothing at .xspec/lock`), the E-6 writer test writing no exchange and the Windows byte-identity test failing at the same assertion before consulting one; since it, the writer test passes (12.1 s alone under the `unshare --map-user` recipe with `XSPEC_E6_EXCHANGE_DIR` set) and, on Linux, the byte-identity test passes against that exchange (`npm run test:windows`, 38.5 s, the drive-mismatch test failing there by design), as it does on the Windows CI leg (run 1280 at fca8af0: 3 files, 9 tests, all passing, in 46.95 s). The cross-leg comparison reproduces on Linux with a product modelling the lock directory: the scratch stand-in `t9j2_48/standin.mjs <mode> <binJs> <argv...>` (rebuild it from this description if it is gone) wraps the built product — an acquiring invocation creates `.xspec/lock` and its entry `<pid>-<16 hex>`, refuses `workspace-busy` (exit 2, the error document under `--json`) when another entry's identifier is alive by `process.kill(pid, 0)`, else removes every other occupant, runs the product with stdio inherited, and releases — in modes `conform`, `noentry`, `alive`, `dead`, `noremove`, `keep`, `keepmove`, `keepcreate`, `keepresolve`, `wrongcode`, `wrongpath`, `slowbusy`, `busywrite`, `alivefirst` (refuses the first `rename` once, its state file `$E6_STANDIN_STATE`), and `adopt` (keeps a dead leftover as its own entry); `t9j2_48/run_zz.sh <log name>` runs the fixture against it through a temporary `test/self/zz-t9j2-48.test.ts` (copied from `zz-t9j2-48.test.ts.saved` and always removed; outcomes appended to `t9j2_48/outcomes.log`), with `ZZ_MODES=<m,…>` (`built` for the built product), `ZZ_FORCE_VOID=1` (a `vi.mock` of `helpers/e6-exclusion.js` voids the reuse check's first call; with `ZZ_VOID_ALL=1` every call), `ZZ_EXCHANGE_WRITE=<dir>`, and `ZZ_EXCHANGE_COMPARE=<dir>`: `conform` passes (~11.5 s, 26 steps); the built product and `noentry` fail after the kill; `alive` and `alivefirst` at the reuse check (none listed); `dead` and `wrongcode` at the busy document's code, `wrongpath` at its path, `slowbusy` at the 15 s bound, `busywrite` at the held-state byte half, `noremove` at its count half, `adopt` at the named-apart check, and each `keep*` at the absence after its command; `alivefirst` with a forced void passes after one restore, its outputs byte-identical to a `conform` exchange; and `alive` with every call voided ends in `VoidedTrialsExhaustedError` after 5 attempts. - Local-only suite (TEST-SPEC E-2; separately invocable, never run in CI, currently empty): `npm run test:local`.
- Property tests (TEST-SPEC 16; machinery in `test/helpers/property.ts`) run a fixed seed set by default — the CI mode, fully deterministic. To rerun with a specific seed: `XSPEC_PROPERTY_SEED=<uint32 from the failure message>`. Optional randomized local mode: `XSPEC_PROPERTY_SEED=random` (each property reports its seed for replay). Never set the variable in CI. Vitest intercepts the seed reports (`console.info`); add `--disable-console-intercept` to the vitest invocation to see them — but place any test-file filter argument *before* that flag (a file path following `--disable-console-intercept` is not treated as a filter and the whole project runs).
- Measuring what the fixed CI seeds actually stage through a section-16 module's private generators (e.g. P-1's `segmentCandidate`/`tagsValueCandidate` in `test/suite/registry/section-16-p1.ts`): copy the module minus its registered test (`sed '/^const P_1 = defineProductTest/,$d'`) to a `*.tmp.ts` twin beside it, append an `export { … }` of the generators and oracle functions, and drive `drawFixedSeedTrials(generator, 25)` (`test/helpers/property.ts`; 25 = the default runs per seed) from a temporary self-test (pattern above) that classifies the draws and prints counts through `console.info` under `--disable-console-intercept` — the way to confirm a generator change still reaches every certified flip class and every staging shape before running the certification; delete both files before committing (nothing imports the twin, but `tsc -p test` and Prettier would see it). P-1 itself runs ~35 s against the built product on the default seed set (150 `build` invocations) and ~15 s under `XSPEC_PROPERTY_SEED=random` (one seed per property). To count a violator's flip class in that temporary self-test, re-judge each draw with the twin's own `segmentsVerdict`/`tagsVerdict` after replacing the violator's deviating code points by `a` (no forbidden name contains `a`, and `a` neither splits a segment nor a tag): a draw is in VIOL-VALID-SEP's class when the oracle rejects it and accepts it with U+2028 and U+2029 replaced, in VIOL-VALID-CTRL's likewise for U+0000-U+0008, U+000E-U+001F, and U+007F, and in VIOL-VALID-WIDE's when the oracle accepts it and it holds U+00A0 or U+0085. The fixed seeds' P-1 counts since the re-descent's FIX_PLAN Task 3 (U+2028 and U+2029 moved into the invalid quote-and-escape group at weight 10 each, U+00A0 and U+0085 staying the valid boundaries at weight 5 each), 75 draws per property: segment draws: 11 hold U+2028 and 10 hold U+2029; SEP's class 5 (3 holding U+2028, 2 holding U+2029), WIDE's 6 (4 holding U+00A0, 3 holding U+0085), CTRL's 4; 19 accepted. Tag draws: 11 hold U+2028 and 9 hold U+2029; SEP's class 7 (4 and 4), WIDE's 3 (2 and 1), CTRL's 8; 33 accepted. Equal weights 3 to 8 left U+2029 at most one SEP-class segment draw (none at 3), and 3 to 5 none among the tag draws. The segment property falsifies first at seed 271828183: CTRL at trial 22 (shrunk to a lone U+0000), WIDE at trial 2 (shrunk to `aaa`, U+00A0, `.a`), and SEP's class first at trial 11 (`a`, U+2028, `0b`), where the built product, which predates 1.4's bar on the two code points, fails P-1 diagnosed (shrunk to a lone U+2028; ~14 s).
- P-5's fixed-seed section moves and their draw guard (the eleventh plan's FIX_PLAN Task 14; TEST-SPEC §16 P-5, E-5): `test/self/p5-fixed-seed-draws.test.ts` replays `drawFixedSeedTrials(genSectionMoveTrial, P5_SECTION_MOVE_RUNS)` — P-5's arm-2 generator and its registered 8 runs per seed, both exported by `test/suite/registry/section-16-p5-p6.ts` — and requires every `TEXT_POSITION_SHAPES` member drawn at least once (a single-line section holding prose moved into a text-position target parent of that shape). At the fixed seeds 6 of the 24 trials route there: `laterLine` 3 (seed 271828183, trials 5, 7, and 8), `selfClosing` 2 (seed 271828183 trial 6, seed 161803399 trial 1), and `sameLine` 1 (seed 161803399 trial 8); seed 314159265 routes none (most of its trials draw an import-adding move first). Unbiased, none of the 24 could take the routing (7 of the 24 models held no section whose collapse holds prose, none held one beside a valid target admitting a paired shape, and the trials over the 3 holding one beside a valid empty target each drew another move), hence the module's `TEXT_POSITION_BIAS` (0.4 of the trials drawing no import-adding move) and `TEXT_POSITION_ROUTING` (0.9); the module header's "the target side" paragraph says how a bound trial is drawn. A trial that draws no new choice keeps its draws, but every later trial of its seed shifts once one does: P-5's falsifying trial (seed 271828183, trial 1, an import-adding move) is unchanged, its counterexample identical but for the rendered `textPositionTarget` field. All six passed `runSectionMoveTrial` against the built product, run from a temporary self-test over the twin (~10 s, with an S-9 `deriveMdx` and oracle pass over all 24 draws). To re-measure, use the twin recipe above; the twin must not re-export `genSectionMoveTrial`, `TextPositionShape`, `stagedSectionMoveSources`, `P5_WOULD_BE_LABEL_PREFIX`, `FLOW_LAYOUT`, or the decoration constants `LEAD_OUTSIDE`, `LEAD_INSIDE`, `TAIL_INSIDE`, `TAIL_OUTSIDE`, `WS_RESIDUE`, and `TAB_RESIDUE`, which the module exports, and a twin and the module itself cannot load in one Vitest process (the staged-source ledger, `test/helpers/staged-ts.ts`, refuses the second load's duplicate record name), so compare the two in separate runs. Should the guard fail after a generator change (P-5's, or PROP-03's `genWorkspaceModel`, which shifts every stream), re-weight the bias or routing and re-measure; never weaken the guard. Since the twelfth plan's FIX_PLAN Task 10 the file holds a second test, S-9's per-draw replay: P-5's arm 2 run through `checkProperty` as registered — `genSectionMoveTrial`, the fixed seeds (no `seeds`, `env: {}`), `P5_SECTION_MOVE_RUNS`, and `drawSources: stagedSectionMoveSources` — with a body that only counts, so every fixed-seed draw's staged files and would-be texts derive before any product exists (P-5 itself stops at its first falsified trial), each of the 24 draws yielding at least one would-be text (~0.2 s of test time, ~2 s with Vitest's start-up). - Format code (Prettier, default config, `src/` and `test/` only): `npm run format`; verify: `npm run format:check`.
- CI: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — harness-self (Linux), full suite (Linux; both Linux jobs run through `.github/scripts/run-without-network.sh`: network disabled after setup, the runner's own unprivileged identity, the job's passwordless sudo kept), and the Windows E-6 leg on every pull request. The harness-self job installs no product: it does not build, and a step confirms `dist/` absent before the self project and certification run (TEST-SPEC H-8), so a self-test or certification that needs the built product fails there; the full-suite and Windows jobs build it first. Each Linux job's wrapped step opens with the wrapper's verification line; on the hosted `ubuntu-24.04` runner (run of 8d20bdb) it read `uid 1001, gid 1001, groups 1001,4,100,118,999; no capabilities; the caller's resource limits; network: lo alone; administrative access: sudo; temporary directory /tmp on ext2/ext3` (`ext2/ext3` is `stat -f`'s name for ext4's magic), and no sudo warning followed. The `e6-linux-outputs` upload step of the full-suite job runs under `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` (with `if-no-files-found: ignore`), so the exchange the E-6 writer test wrote is uploaded even when other Linux tests fail — only a cancelled job, or one that died before its suite step, ends with no artifact: the Windows byte-identity verdict is meaningful whenever the Linux writer test completed, not only on a fully green Linux run, and that test fails loudly on the missing manifest exactly when no exchange was written. Job time limits (`timeout-minutes`): harness-self 20, full suite 90, Windows 30 — limits of the CI service, not harness guards (TEST-SPEC S-3). The full-suite job took up to 34 minutes on the slower hosted-runner class (green runs 1286–1332), with the twenty new tests, P-16, and new arms of TEST-SPEC's Phase 6 HALT at 80b83aa not yet implemented. Re-measure once a job passes ~75% of its limit.
- Reading a CI run from this sandbox: `gh` here is Claude Code's built-in GitHub client, not the GitHub CLI, and `gh api <REST endpoint>` reaches api.github.com through the session's GitHub proxy (confirmed at the third plan's FIX_PLAN Task 11). `gh api 'repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs?branch=claude/xspec-ui-apis-4df8fa&per_page=5' --jq '.workflow_runs[] | [.id, .run_number, .head_sha[0:7], .status, .conclusion] | @tsv'` lists the branch's runs, `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/<run-id>/jobs` gives each job's and step's status and conclusion, and `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/check-runs/<job-id>/annotations` a job's annotations (a job's ID is its check run's); the pulls and branches endpoints answer too. It refuses the log download's redirect (to a `*.blob.core.windows.net` host), so `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/jobs/<job-id>/logs` fails by design. The GitHub MCP tools fetch logs: `get_job_logs` (`job_id`, `return_content: false`) returns one job's signed `logs_url` on `productionresultssa<N>.blob.core.windows.net` (valid ~10 min; the plain-text log, 172 KB for a green harness-self job), and `actions_get`'s `get_workflow_run_logs_url` (the run's ID) a signed URL on `results-receiver.actions.githubusercontent.com` for a zip holding one `<n>_<job name>.txt` log per job (0.3 MB for a green run). Each URL arrives JSON-escaped, every ampersand spelled as the six-character JSON escape of U+0026: turn each into `&` (build the escape from character codes, e.g. Python's `chr(92) + 'u0026'`, since the tool-parameter layer may decode that spelling), and `curl -sS -o <file> '<url>'` fetches it through the proxy. A job no hosted runner acquires ends `cancelled` after ~15 min with no steps and the annotation "The job was not acquired by Runner of type hosted even after multiple attempts" (run 887's `suite-linux` at 008d1e1), and the Windows leg then fails on the missing `e6-linux-outputs` artifact, by design: an infrastructure event, not a harness result, so read a cancelled job's annotations before reading it as a verdict. A push to the branch cancels the branch's run in progress (`concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress`), so a run completes only when no later push lands within ~13–29 min (run 642 at 8f5660d: `harness-self` 2 min; A CI log's lines carry a timestamp prefix and ANSI colour codes (Vitest colours its output under `CI`), and its `×` lines carry the bare test title with no `file > ` path, so the failed-ID recipe of the fourth-plan Task 24 bullet (which greps the `×` lines of a local `--reporter=verbose` log for `> ID`) finds nothing on it. On a CI log, strip the colour codes and take the IDs from Vitest's ` FAIL ` summary lines instead: `sed -E 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' <log> | grep -E ' FAIL +suite ' | grep -oE '> (T[0-9.]+-[0-9]+|P-[0-9]+) ' | sed -E 's/^> //; s/ $//' | sort -u`. The `suite` project badge keeps out the self project's failures (` FAIL   self `, read the same way) and the certification runner's per-pair `  FAIL  T…` lines (a violator's expected outcomes, which carry no `> `). Checked on run 33275585205's `suite-linux` log (98 failed): 98 ` FAIL   suite ` lines and 97 IDs, the one line without an ID being the E-6 writer test's (`test/suite/e6-exchange-writer.test.ts > E-6 Linux leg: …`); run 642's green log holds no ` FAIL ` summary line at all. In a CI log Vitest's closing summary (`Test Files`, `Tests`, `Start at`, `Duration`) need not follow the last failure block: in run 1253's full-suite log it landed after the 15th of the `Failed Tests` section's 29 blocks (run 1246's came after the last), so a reader of that section takes every ` FAIL ` block through the end of the log rather than stopping at the summary.
- Answer-document scale (TEST-SPEC H-11): the suite stages section towers 4096 deep (`NESTING_DEPTHS` in `test/suite/registry/section-16-p8.ts`), past V8's limits in this Node — a plain recursive function gets ~9.9k frames, and `JSON.stringify`/`structuredClone` throw `RangeError` at that nesting while `JSON.parse` is iterative. Harness walks over answer documents therefore use explicit stacks (`decodeViewNodeForm`, `assertUnavailabilityMarkerForms`, `describeJsonValue`'s fallback, and `query.ts`'s `walkForRangeData` and `decodeIdsTreeNode` — `ids --tree` nests one node per section level — in `test/helpers/adapters/`, and the registry modules' own generic JSON walkers, `canonicalJson`, `collectStringLeaves` and `canonicalizeJson` in `test/suite/registry/section-10.*.ts` and `section-12.0-i.ts`); a property reporting `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` as a harness error names a walk still recursing per level — its `Caused by` frames locate it. To drive a decoder at depth by hand, a temporary self-test (see above) building the document in a loop is enough: 200k-deep `ids --tree` and edge documents decode in well under a second. A walker its module does not export can be exercised the same way as a scratch `.ts` twin of it run under `node --experimental-strip-types` (Node 22); `deriveMdx(source)` answers `{ derives: true }` or `{ derives: false, reason, position? }`.
- Staged-scale gates (TEST-SPEC S-2, S-8): `test/self/staged-scale.ts` derives the suite's staged input maxima from what the suite stages, per kind. - Checking whether a staged MDX shape is well-formed (SPEC 14.20) before pinning it in a fixture: the harness declares the stock MDX 3 parser as its own devDependencies (`micromark` with `micromark-extension-mdxjs`, `mdast-util-from-markdown` with `mdast-util-mdx` — TEST-SPEC S-9 needs a means independent of the product's `remark-mdx`), so from the repository root `node --input-type=module -e 'import { fromMarkdown } from "mdast-util-from-markdown"; import { mdxjs } from "micromark-extension-mdxjs"; import { mdxFromMarkdown } from "mdast-util-mdx"; fromMarkdown(TEXT, { extensions: [mdxjs()], mdastExtensions: [mdxFromMarkdown()] })'` throws where the stock grammar rejects the shape (bare specifiers resolve from the working directory for `-e`; a script under the scratchpad cannot resolve them) — the product's 14.20 verdict up to its documented widenings of that grammar (`src/core/mdx.ts`). The product's own verdict needs no workspace: a scratch `.mjs` importing `parseSpecSource` (or `specSourceParseFailure`, the verdict alone) from `/home/user/xspec/dist/core/mdx.js` by absolute path prints a text's 14.20 finding or its document model — every section's `range`, `openingTagRange`, and `closingTagRange`, and the findings — in milliseconds (a 4096-deep tower parses in ~0.3 s). JSX tag matching lives in the mdast layer: the tokenizer alone (`postprocess(parse({ extensions: [mdxjs()] }).document().write(preprocess()(TEXT, "utf8", true)))` from `micromark`) accepts an unclosed or mismatched tag that the full parse, and the product, reject. Beware CommonMark's block structure, which the CONF-MD conformer's hand-rolled lexer does not model: a paragraph-continuation line whose first non-whitespace character is `>` interrupts as a block quote whatever its indentation (MDX disables indented code), so a text-context multi-line JSX tag cannot close on a bare `>` line, while a tag opening at line start can (the concrete JSX flow attempt). An ESM block interrupts no paragraph and runs to a blank line: an import line following text without a blank line between is paragraph text, one directly followed by a non-blank line fails acorn, and two imports on one physical line separated by U+2028 or U+2029 derive as one block with a blank line on each side (acorn reads the ECMAScript LineTerminator; automatic semicolon insertion applies). The harness's own entry for that check is `deriveMdx` in `test/helpers/mdx-derivability.ts` (bytes or a string; `{ allowances: [...] }` names the S-9 early-error allowances of `MDX_ALLOWANCES` a source relies on, applied inside the parse so a later rejection still surfaces; the verdict is `{ derives: true }` or `{ derives: false, reason, position? }`); its self-test runs alone, no namespace needed, with `npx vitest run --config test/vitest.config.ts --project self test/self/s9-fixture-well-formedness.test.ts` (~0.5 s); it judges T3-1's and T6.2-3's staged sources verbatim, imported from their registry modules (`REMOVALS_SOURCE` in `test/suite/registry/section-3.ts`; `I3_ROOM_SOURCE` and the two post-move files in `section-6.2.ts`), so a restaging of either fixture is checked by that single file before any product runs (the self project can import registry modules: `defineProductTest` only builds a frozen entry). The workspace builder (`test/helpers/workspace.ts`) applies that same check to every staged file whose path ends in `.mdx`, at staging time (`TestWorkspace.create` and `file()` alike, before the bytes are written): well-formed is the default, and a staging declares the exceptions by workspace-relative path in `mdx: { unparseable: [...], unchecked: [...], allowances: { "<path>": [...] } }` on the `create` declaration (it also governs later `file()` calls on those paths) or per call as `file(path, contents, { mdx: "well-formed" | "unparseable" | "unchecked" | { allowances: [...] } })`; a source contradicting its declaration throws `HarnessStagingError` (mode `mdx-derivability`, the message naming the path and the parser's reason and position) — a harness error the S-7 sweep, the certification runner, and the suite report as such, never a diagnosed product failure and never a skip — so every 14.20 fixture (invalid UTF-8, a byte-order mark, a syntax rejection) needs its `unparseable` entry, every early-error form its allowance, and `unchecked` is only for fuzz mutations and noise files whose derivability TEST-SPEC does not declare (never a way to hide an ill-formed fixture; S-9). The parse is in-process and cheap at the suite's scale (the 4096-deep tower ~0.3 s, the 4.2 MB deterministic maximum ~1.4 s), so no staging is exempted for size; a staging refused inside `create` leaves no temporary directory behind. Its identifier characters — expressions', ESM blocks', JSX element and attribute names', private names', and RegExp group names' — and its whitespace are Unicode 15.1's, judged code point by code point (FIX_PLAN Task 17; S-9, SPEC 14.20): TypeScript 5.9.3's ESNext tables (`ts.isIdentifierStart`/`isIdentifierPart` of `typescript-5.9.3`, equal to Unicode 15.1's ID_Start/ID_Continue), never acorn 8.17's (Unicode 17) nor the runtime's (Unicode 17 on Node 22.22.2) — so an identifier or JSX name holding U+1C89 (a Unicode 16 letter) does not derive, its staging needing an `unparseable` entry, while U+2EBF0 (a 15.1 letter, astral) derives in a JSX element or attribute name as in an expression. acorn's name, private-name, and JSX-name tokens are held to 15.1 as they finish (`Unicode151Parser`), and the MDX tag tokenizer sees each non-ASCII code point inside an open tag through a stand-in of its 15.1 class (`withUnicode151Jsx`, an astral code point read whole from the text at micromark's offset), its rejection messages naming the actual character `(U+XXXX, judged by Unicode 15.1)`; `deriveMdx` throws a plain `Error` — a harness error, never a verdict — on a runtime whose `\s` class is not Unicode 15.1's, since the stock empty-expression judgement reads it. That block of the self-test runs alone with `-t 'Unicode 15.1'` on the file (71 tests, ~1 s, half of it the scan confirming acorn admits every 15.1 identifier character); stashing the helper alone (the red-check recipe above) fails 27 of them.
- Checking whether a staged TypeScript shape — a code source or a configuration file — is well-formed (SPEC 14.20) before pinning it in a fixture (FIX_PLAN Task 14; TEST-SPEC S-9's TypeScript clause): the harness's judge is `judgeTypeScript(source, name)` in `test/helpers/ts-derivability.ts` (bytes or a decoded string, and the file name), which uses `typescript-5.9.3`'s parser at ESNext. A name ending `.tsx` parses as TSX and every other name as plain TypeScript; the parser is given a neutral name of that kind, so a `.d.ts` name is plain TypeScript too, never TypeScript's ambient declaration-file parse. Each text is read twice, as module code and as script code, by forcing the module indicator on and off through `createSourceFile`'s `setExternalModuleIndicator`. Only the parse's own diagnostics count (scanner and parser): no program, binder, or checker is created. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8, or that begin with a byte-order mark, are unparseable (SPEC 1.6). The verdict is `{ verdict: "well-formed" }`, `{ verdict: "unparseable", reason, errors }`, or `{ verdict: "one-way", accepts, reason, errors }`; `errors` lists each reading's diagnostics, each located by UTF-16 index, byte offset, and 1-based line and column. `tsDeclarationProblem(verdict, "well-formed" | "unparseable")` returns the harness error's text, or undefined when the verdict agrees with the declaration. A one-way text is a problem under either declaration; the top-level `await` forms are the cases (`await /re/;` is accepted as module code only, `let a = await / 2 / 1;` as script code only). Quick probe with no build: a scratch `.mts` that imports `judgeTypeScript` from `/home/user/xspec/test/helpers/ts-derivability.ts` by absolute path runs under `node --experimental-strip-types --no-warnings <file>.mts` and prints a verdict in milliseconds. The self-test runs alone, no namespace needed: `npx vitest run --config test/vitest.config.ts --project self test/self/s9-typescript-well-formedness.test.ts` (56 tests, ~2 s with start-up). TypeScript 5.9.3 facts the vectors rely on: it parses `await x` as an await expression outside an await context too, so that text is accepted both ways and left to the checker. It scans U+200B, U+0085, and a non-leading U+FEFF as whitespace. At ESNext it admits U+2EBF0 in identifiers (ES5 does not), but never U+1C89 (TS1127 at its first byte). Its scanner rejects `010` (TS1121) and `09` (TS1489) at the literal's first digit. An invalid `/// <reference …/>` directive (TS1084) is one of the parse's own diagnostics. It accepts `using` and `await using` declarations both ways wherever they stand — at a file's top level too (`using f = () => {};`, `await using h = () => {};`), and inside an async function — so a staging of either form needs no `ts` declaration (FIX_PLAN Task 22's T1.7-2 `src/using.ts` and T4.6-1 arms). The workspace builder (`test/helpers/workspace.ts`) applies this check at staging time (FIX_PLAN Task 15), through the same four stagings as the `.mdx` check (`TestWorkspace.create`'s initial files, `file()`, `edit()`, `copyFrom()`), before the bytes are written: every file whose name ends in one of `TS_DEFAULT_SUFFIXES` (`.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mts`, `.cts`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs` — so `.d.ts` names, `xspec.config.ts`, and every `--config` target the suite stages, all named `.ts`) is declared well-formed by default, and a staging declares the exceptions by workspace-relative path (keyed and normalized as the `mdx` declaration's keys) in `ts: { unparseable: [...], unchecked: [...], wellFormed: [...], perDraw: [...] }` on the `create` declaration (it also governs later `file()`, `edit()`, and `copyFrom()` stagings of those paths) or per call as `file(path, contents, { ts: "well-formed" | "unparseable" | "unchecked" | "per-draw" })` (`perDraw` and `"per-draw"` since FIX_PLAN Task 16o: a property draw's composed configuration or code source, judged well-formed at staging and exempt from the undeclared-staging guard's TypeScript arm, section-16 modules only); a path in two lists is refused at creation. `unparseable` is for a file TEST-SPEC declares unparseable or malformed (T1.6-5's encodings, T7-2's syntax-error and encoding configurations, T11.6-4's, T12.6-2's, and T12.7-3's malformed configurations, T14-3's and T14-5's TSX-only constructs, T14-11's (m) and (v) code sources, every code-source arm of T14-12 wherever it is staged — `unparseableDecl` and T14-11's `reassertedCase` derive it from the arm's `kind`), `unchecked` for one whose well-formedness the document does not declare (P-8's and P-11's mutated code sources and configuration, T13.4-2's truncated and garbage-overwritten derived files, T13.4-4's noise at the generated module's path, and since FIX_PLAN Task 16i T7.5-6's tampered generated module — product-written bytes plus a harness comment, staged by `file()` with `{ ts: "unchecked" }`, and since FIX_PLAN Task 16l T12.2-2's and T12.2-4 (a)'s likewise), and `wellFormed` for a code source whose name the default does not reach (a code group globs any name: §11.4's `docs/impl.mdx` — T2.1-2's `docs/EXTRA.mdx` carries its declaration in its MDX record's `ts` since FIX_PLAN Task 16b, T7.3-1's `specs/A.md` (well-formed) and T7-6's `specs/a'b.md` holding `)` (`unparseable`) are `StagedTs` records carrying theirs since FIX_PLAN Task 16h, and T7.5-5's `src/end$` and `src/end` share one well-formed `StagedTs` record (`CODE_MARKER_TO_P`) since FIX_PLAN Task 16i, and T13.4-11(b)'s `specs/A.md` is a well-formed `StagedTs` record since FIX_PLAN Task 16l, a record making its path judged). A contradiction — and a text accepted read one way only, under any declaration but `unchecked` — throws `HarnessStagingError` (mode `ts-derivability`, naming the path, the verdict's first TypeScript error, and the remedy), a harness error the S-7 sweep, the certification runner, and the suite report as such; `tsDeclarationOf(path)` reads back the declaration in effect (undefined for a path nothing judges), and `judgeTsDeclaration(key, bytes, declaration)` is the one code path. The S-2 self-test (`test/self/s2-workspace-builder.test.ts`, 21 tests) carries the builder's TypeScript vectors. Finding every staging a builder check judges in one pass, instead of one harness error per run: temporarily make the private `checkTs` (or `checkMdx`) append one JSON line per judged staging — path, declaration, the judge's verdict, `this.invocationMark.invoked`, and the running body's ID (`product-invocations.ts` keeps it in an `AsyncLocalStorage`; export a getter for the run) — to a scratch file and return instead of throwing, run the self project (S-7's sweep reaches every body's pre-invocation stagings) and the suite once each, and revert the edit.
